answer: The protocol validates identities by enforcing a memory-hard work requirement where each agent must dedicate 1,000 gigabytes of non-swappable RAM as an atlas of state. An issuer acts as a cipher verifier, checking that no two agents overlap in their allocated memory windows to ensure capacity exclusivity. A signal of conflicting usage triggers an immediate stake slash, with no refund. Honest agents pay for one unit; 1,000 fakes pay 1,000 times as much.
